Figure 1:KGO consists of four main parts. (Left) A representation learning stage transforms the input time series via RevIN normalization, patching, and an sLSTM encoder into a latent state.
(Middle-left) Koopman Patch Embedding (KoPE) extrapolates latent states by applying powers of a learned linear operator in latent space.
(Middle-right, top) A residual MLP (ResMLP) decodes the KoPE latents into a deterministic point forecast. (Middle-right, bottom) Koopman Flow Matching (KoFM) generates probabilistic forecasts by interpolating between noise and data and transporting samples through a matrix exponential conditioned on the KoPE latents. (Right) An Adaptive Uncertainty Gate (AUG) combines deterministic and probabilistic predictions for the final forecast. Extended details in App.A.

Figure 7:Eigenvalues of the learned KoPE operator𝐊\mathbf{K}on the nine long-term datasets, pooled over the four horizons (seed 0); the dashed circle is the unit circle. Color encodes|λ||\lambda|on each panel’s own range, given by the bar below the panel. The isolated high-magnitude modes outside the bulk include the seasonal modes discussed in App.F.2.1.

Figure 8:Gate weights averaged over the test windows (seed 0) for eight dataset–horizon pairs, named in the panel titles. Within each panel, the horizontal axis indexes variates and the vertical axis indexes forecast steps, increasing from bottom to top. Color encodes the stochastic weight on the panel’s own range, from its lowest value (amber; the 1st percentile for Traffic-L and Electricity-L, whose few lowest cells would otherwise wash out the rest) to its highest (navy), given by the bar below the panel.
